summary: This note is the message definition for LaserScan, a single scan from a planar laser range-finder in the ROS robotics ecosystem. It describes the header timestamp convention, the angular and timing fields (angle_min, angle_max, angle_increment, time_increment, scan_time), the range limits and range array, and the optional intensities array. It also notes that other ranging devices such as sonar arrays should use a different message because applications make laser-specific assumptions.
one_line: Defines the LaserScan message format for a single scan from a planar laser range-finder, including angles, timing, ranges and intensities.
key_facts: LaserScan is a single scan from a planar laser range-finder.
Other ranging devices with different behavior, such as a sonar array, should use a different message because applications make fairly laser-specific assumptions.
The header timestamp is the acquisition time of the first ray in the scan.
Angles are measured in the frame given by frame_id, around the positive Z axis (counterclockwise if Z is up), with zero angle being forward along the x axis.
angle_min is the start angle of the scan in radians.
angle_max is the end angle of the scan in radians.
angle_increment is the angular distance between measurements in radians.
time_increment is the time between measurements in seconds and is used to interpolate 3D point positions if the scanner is moving.
scan_time is the time between scans in seconds.
range_min is the minimum range value in meters.
range_max is the maximum range value in meters.
The ranges field holds range data in meters.
Range values less than range_min or greater than range_max should be discarded.
The intensities field holds intensity data in device-specific units.
If a device does not provide intensities, the intensities array should be left empty.
